IDQ20809
Australian Government Bureau of Meteorology

Final Flood Warning for the Bremer River and Warrill Creek

Issued at 8:51 am AEST on Saturday 24 October 2026
Flood Warning Number: 6


FLOODING NO LONGER OCCURRING ALONG BREMER RIVER AND WARRILL CREEK

On Friday evening river levels along the Bremer River fell below the minor flood level at
Rosewood and peaked just below the minor flood level at Five Mile Bridge.

Early Saturday morning river levels along the Warrill Creek fell below the minor flood
level at Amberley.

Further showers and thunderstorms are forecast across the Bremer River and Warrill Creek
over the weekend. The situation will be monitored and warnings reissued as required.

Warrill Creek:
Flooding is no longer occurring along Warrill Creek.


The Warrill Creek at Amberley peaked at 5.22 m around 03:15 pm Friday 23 October, with
minor flooding, and fell below the minor flood level (4.00 metres) early Saturday morning.
The creek is currently at 3.52 m and falling, below the minor flood level. The Warrill
Creek at Amberley is expected to fall below the minor flood level (4.00 m) during Saturday
24 October.

Bremer River:
Flooding is no longer occurring along the Bremer River.

The Bremer River at Rosewood peaked at 4.17 m around 02:00 pm Friday 23 October, with
minor flooding, and fell below the minor flood level (4.00 metres) Friday evening. The
river is currently at 3.02 m and falling, below the minor flood level. The Bremer River at
Rosewood is expected to remain below the minor flood level (4.00 m).

The Bremer River at Five Mile Bridge peaked at 3.38 m around 10:30 pm Friday 23 October,
just below the minor flood level (3.50 metres). The river is currently at 3.06 m and
falling, below the minor flood level. The Bremer River at Five Mile Bridge is expected to
remain below the minor flood level (3.50 m).

Safety Advice:
* Don't drive, walk, swim or play in floodwater because it is dangerous.
* Stay away from flooded drains, rivers, streams and waterways.
* Obey road closure signs. Plan ahead so you don't drive on flooded roads.
* Check the ABC and local media for updates. The situation can change quickly, so stay
informed.
* For local emergency management warnings and advice visit
www.disaster.qld.gov.au/warnings.

For emergency assistance call SES on telephone number 132 500. In life-threatening
emergencies, call 000 (triple zero) immediately.

Next issue:
This is a final warning. No further warnings will be issued for this event.
